message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or agree on a different target). Points come from the cards left in opponents’ hands when you finish a round. | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each (one 0, two 1‑9, two “Draw Two”, two “Skip”, two “Reverse”), plus 4 “Wild” and 4 “Wild Draw Four”. | | **Setup** | Shuffle the deck. Deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. | | **Turn order** | Players sit around the table. The first turn goes clockwise; a “Reverse” changes direction. | | **Playing a card** | On your turn you may play one card that matches either the color or the number/symbol of the top discard. If you have no playable card, you must draw one from the draw pile. If that drawn card is playable, you may play it immediately. | | **Special cards** | • **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction (acts like Skip if only two players).
• **Wild** – You choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – You choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. (Can be challenged if the challenged player has a matching color.) | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you play your second‑to‑last card, shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player calls it out, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a round** | The first player to discard all their cards wins the round. | | **Scoring** | Add up the point values of the cards still held by the other players:
• Number cards = face value
• Draw Two, Skip, Reverse = 20 points each
• Wild, Wild Draw Four = 50 points each
• Winner gets those points added to their total. | | **Game end** | First player to reach the agreed‑upon score (e.g., 500) wins the game. | **Optional house rules** - *Stacking*: Some groups allow stacking Draw Twos or Wild Draw Fours (next player adds to the stack instead of drawing). - *No challenge*: Others forbid challenging Wild Draw Fours. - *Custom scoring*: You can set a different target score or use a “hand‑in” rule where the winner of a round collects the cards in the discard pile. That’s the core of Uno—simple, fast, and full of surprises!
